rules: candidates: kurl notes and published blog posts written in [asOf - 7 days, asOf]; remote posts received in [asOf - 72 hours, asOf] and written at or after asOf - 72 hours, the 1,000 with the highest noteId
a remote candidate whose noteId is a kurl note's id is dropped for the kurl note; a key or remote noteId seen twice is used once, the first wins
E = likes + 2*reposts + replies (negatives as 0); ageHours = whole seconds from createdAt to asOf, at least 0, / 3600; a blog post's createdAt is its publishing time
lang: 0 when the reader has no language, 0.5 when the post's language is unknown, else 1 if the post's primary language subtag (lowercase) is one of the reader's, else 0

interest = 1 - (1 - topic)(1 - author); author = min(1, authors[author] / 3); topic = cosine between the reader's tag weights times idf and the post's tags times idf, idf = ln(1 + N / postsWithTag) over the ranked pool (candidates after windows and duplicates, without my posts, seen ones included), tags lowercase
follow: 1 when a signed-in reader follows the author (kurl or remote), else 0; local: 1 for kurl posts
ties: newer createdAt first, then key ascending

diversity over the ranked order: in each block of 20, at most 2 per author and 10 per server, kurl counting as one server; when nothing eligible is left the server cap gives way first, then the author cap; the list stops at 400

my posts (signed-in reader is the kurl author): at most 60 minutes old at asOf and not seen before asOf, they sit above the ranking, newest first, outside the blocks; every other post of mine is left out; a device has no posts of its own
seen=hide leaves out any candidate the same viewer saw before asOf (kurl:note:{id}, kurl:post:{id}, remote uri); without it nothing seen is left out and my recent posts stay pinned
ranking, idf and the pool use only what was there at asOf: a page with a cursor continues the same list, so sightings or posts arriving after asOf move nothing and pages neither overlap nor skip
pages are slices of limit over the pinned posts followed by the ranking

format.asOf: the first page's time; every page of the scroll uses it
format.reader: viewer {kind member|device, id}, languages, tags {tag: weight}, authors {author: weight}, follows [author]
format.candidates: key, source kurl-note|kurl-post|remote, noteId (kurl note id, or a remote post's stored note id; null for blog posts), userId (kurl author), author, host (remote), language, tags, createdAt, receivedAt (remote), likes, reposts, replies; for a blog post the backend decides which counts stand for likes, reposts and replies
format.seen: sightings {viewer, key, at}; only those before asOf by the same viewer count
format.expected.order: the whole list: pinned posts, then the ranking
format.expected.pages: what each page returns at the case's limit; the last page has no next cursor
format.expected.scores: score of every ranked candidate (seen ones included), rounded to 6 decimals; compare within 1e-6
format.expected.excluded: why a candidate is not in the list: window, pool-size, duplicate (key suffixed #remote or #again), mine-old, mine-seen, seen, past-cap

cases.name: a post that just came in beats a day-old one with ten reactions
a day-old post with fifty reactions edges out one that just came in with none
the same reactions: the newer post wins
boosts count twice and replies once
a foreign post gone viral beats a quiet one in the reader's language
a foreign post with some reactions loses to the reader's language
an unknown language sits between the reader's and a foreign one
a reader with no language gets no language term at all
a followed author's quiet post beats a stranger's with a few reactions
following counts for a kurl author too
a signed-out device gets no follow term
the kurl bonus lifts a quiet kurl note over a remote one with a single like
the kurl bonus does not hold against two reactions
a kurl blog post is scored like a note
a pool where nothing has reactions orders by language, kurl and freshness only
equal scores go to the newer post, then the key
a tag the reader cares for lifts a post, a rare one more than a common one
an author the reader keeps reading is lifted, capped at three signals
one loud author gets two in each block of twenty
one server gets ten in each block of twenty
kurl counts as one server for the ten-per-block cap
with nothing else left the caps give way, server first and then author
my note from minutes ago that I have not seen sits on top whatever its score
my posts from the last hour sit on top newest first, then the ranking
my note from just over an hour ago is left out
my older posts are left out entirely
my recent note once seen is left out, not pinned
without seen=hide my recent note stays pinned even once seen
a signed-out device has no posts of its own: the same note is ranked like any other
pinned posts take the first page's slots and push the ranking on
seen=hide leaves out kurl notes, posts and remote posts seen before asOf
without seen=hide the seen are ranked like everything else
a sighting at or after asOf does not hide anything in this scroll
someone else's sightings hide nothing, and a device's do not hide for the member
a device hides what the device saw
seen note 20 does not hide post 20
a scroll in pages of 1: sightings and posts that come after asOf move nothing, pages never overlap or skip
a scroll in pages of 7: sightings and posts that come after asOf move nothing, pages never overlap or skip
a scroll in pages of 20: sightings and posts that come after asOf move nothing, pages never overlap or skip
the same stored kurl note coming from the other-server side too is used once, as the kurl note
the same remote post twice is used once
windows: kurl posts from the last seven days, remote posts received and written in the last 72 hours
the remote pool is the 1,000 latest kept, and the list stops at 400
an empty pool is one empty page
everything seen is one empty page
